description: NExtSEEK Knowledge Graph — lightweight schema for parser routing decisions

node_types.label: Sample
node_types.description: A biological sample. Property 'type' holds the sample type code (e.g. TIS, CEL, DNA, D.SEQ, NHP, MUS). Samples are linked to each other via DERIVED_FROM, to studies via IN_STUDY.

node_types.label: Study
node_types.description: A research study grouping samples. Property 'title'. Linked to an Investigation via IN_INVESTIGATION.

node_types.label: Investigation
node_types.description: A project grouping one or more studies. Property 'title'. Known values: CSBC, GBM_BTC, Griffith, Impact, MetNet, SRP, Shoulders.

relationships.note: Carries assay and protocol metadata on the relationship (internal_assay_title, protocol_title). Used to traverse from derived data back to source samples.
Links a sample directly to the study it belongs to.
Links a study to its parent investigation/project.

graph_query_triggers: Query scopes to a named Study ('in the GBM study', 'in the Griffith study', 'what samples exist in study X')
Query scopes to a named Investigation or Project ('in the IMPACT project', 'in the SRP investigation', 'what studies are in project X')
Query asks what studies, projects, or investigations contain or relate to something ('what projects have mouse samples', 'which investigations have NHP samples with sequencing')
Query counts or aggregates within a study or investigation scope ('how many samples are in the GBM study', 'how many TIS samples exist across all studies')

Query asks about assay or protocol application by vocabulary name ('processed via Tissue Collection', 'underwent Short Read Sequencing', 'associated with flow cytometry protocol', 'samples that underwent single cell sequencing') — especially when no clean REST endpoint exists for the combination
Query mixes Sample results with Study or Investigation membership in the same output
api_preferred_triggers: Filter-based sample search with resolved sampletype code and/or assay code only, no study/investigation scope → advanced_search endpoint
Samples derived from or associated with a specific UID → /samples/tree/ or /samples/associated/ endpoint
Parent samples that have children of multiple specified types → /samples/parents_by_child_types/ endpoint
PATCH/update on a specific sample UID
Any intent that maps cleanly to a known API endpoint in the catalog
disambiguation_rules: If the query mentions a study or investigation by name → graph_query, even if a sampletype is also present
If the query says 'how many X in study Y' or 'across all studies' → graph_query
If the query says 'how many X' with no study/investigation scope and no time span → API advanced_search (not reporter)
If the query has entity-resolved sampletype + assay codes AND no study/investigation scope AND the assay is used as a keyword attribute filter (not a named assay/protocol traversal) → prefer API

If the query asks for samples 'associated with', 'that underwent', or 'processed via' a named assay or protocol → graph_query (assay metadata lives on DERIVED_FROM relationships, not on sample records; REST endpoints cannot filter on it)
If the query asks for parent samples that have children of multiple types → check API catalog for parents_by_child_types endpoint first; if it exists, prefer API
If the query involves project-level upload counts or statistics over time → reporter (not graph_query)
Investigation titles to recognize (case-insensitive): CSBC, GBM_BTC, GBM, Griffith, Impact, IMPACT, MetNet, SRP, Shoulders
